key: As the days follow days in close succession, as with the seasons duly come the seasons, As each successor fails not his foregoer, so form the lives of these, O great Ordainer.
s: In a hymn that sends Death away from the living, the singer turns to the Ordainer; Sāyaṇa, on 10.18.5, takes the successor who does not forsake his foregoer as a son who does not leave his father by dying first.

evidence.gloss: And as the later one, the son born after, does not abandon the former, the father born before, by dying first: just so, in the very way described, O Dhātṛ, sustainer of all, god of that name, arrange (make) the lives of these living members of our family.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok; ref Rig Veda 10.18.5 and at [854,5] match). Plain sense: hymn 10.18 opens by sending Death (Mṛtyu) away and setting a rampart for the living; Sāyaṇa’s introduction makes verses 1 to 4 Death’s and verse 5 Dhātṛ’s, the Ordainer the verse addresses: faithful. In the Sanskrit packet on 10.18.5 Sāyaṇa glosses aparaḥ as the later-born son and pūrvam as the earlier-born father, whom he does not leave by dying first (pūrvamaraṇena); Wilson’s note repeats this as the comment’s reading. No drift. Revision 353436 dated 2022-10-05 by the Wikisource API. Gate ok.
